title: Levers and pulleys
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card 'Simple machines' covers levers, pulleys and inclined planes and its questions test the inclined plane, so it is broader than the levers and pulleys point the NSW Stage 4 course needs, and it is not from the NSW course.

draft.title: Levers and pulleys
card: A simple machine changes the size or direction of a force. The force you apply is the effort. The weight or resistance you move is the load.
a rigid bar that turns around a fixed point called the fulcrum. The further the effort is from the fulcrum, the smaller the effort needed to lift a load.

a wheel with a rope around it. A single fixed pulley changes the direction of the force, so you pull down to lift a load up. Adding more rope sections around moving pulleys lets a smaller effort lift the load.
A smaller effort has a cost. With a lever or a pulley system, the effort moves through a longer distance than the load does.
draft.remember: Machines trade effort for distance, or change the direction of the force.

a.q: A worker uses a single fixed pulley on a building site to lift a bucket of bricks by pulling down on the rope. What does the pulley do?
opts: Changes the direction of the force
Makes the effort smaller than the load
Removes the need for any effort
a.why: A single fixed pulley lets the worker pull down to lift the load up, so it changes the direction of the force. It does not change the weight of the bucket, and the worker still needs to apply an effort.
a.clue: Think about which way the worker pulls and which way the bucket moves.

b.q: Priya uses a long plank as a lever to lift a heavy rock. The fulcrum is a log under the plank. How can she lift the rock with a smaller effort?
opts: Push down further from the fulcrum
Push down closer to the fulcrum
Use a shorter plank with the same log
Push down for a longer time
b.why: The further the effort is from the fulcrum, the smaller the effort needed. Pushing closer to the fulcrum would need a larger effort. The time spent pushing does not change the effort needed.
b.clue: Where along the plank is it easiest to push?

wants.brief: A lever made of a rigid bar resting on a fulcrum. Label the fulcrum, the effort (a downward arrow on the long end of the bar, far from the fulcrum) and the load (a box on the short end, near the fulcrum).
wants.why: Seeing where the fulcrum, effort and load sit helps students picture how distance from the fulcrum matters.

a.best: Changes the direction of the force

b.best: Push down further from the fulcrum
